entries.headline: Lighthouse Gold upsizes private placement to $6.45 million
entries.dek: Lighthouse Gold increased a private placement announced the day before, citing strong investor demand, with closing expected in early November.
entries.caption: An upsized financing: Lighthouse Gold's private placement now targets up to $6.45 million, the company said, citing investor demand.

sources.title: Lighthouse Gold Upsizes Private Placement to up to $6,450,408 Million

unverified_claims: The company's attribution of the increase to 'strong investor demand' rests on its own characterization.
brief: Lighthouse Gold Inc. (CSE: LGHT) said on October 23, 2026 that it has increased the size of its private placement, first announced October 22, 2026, to up to 35,835,600 units at $0.18 per unit for gross proceeds of up to $6,450,408, citing strong investor demand.

Each unit comprises one common share and one-half of one share purchase warrant. Each whole warrant is exercisable for one additional share at $0.28 for two years from closing. The offering remains subject to regulatory approvals, including that of the Canadian Securities Exchange.

The company said it intends to use the proceeds for exploration and general working capital purposes. Closing is expected on or about November 4, 2026. The release did not name an agent or finder, or disclose insider participation in the offering.
body: Lighthouse Gold Inc. (CSE: LGHT) announced on October 23, 2026 that it has increased the size of a private placement first announced October 22, 2026. The company attributed the increase to strong investor demand.

The offering, originally up to 33,334,000 units at $0.18 per unit for gross proceeds of up to $6,000,120, has been increased to up to 35,835,600 units at the same $0.18 per unit, for gross proceeds of up to $6,450,408.

Each unit comprises one common share and one-half of one share purchase warrant, so two units together carry one whole warrant. Each whole warrant entitles the holder to purchase one additional share at an exercise price of $0.28 for a period of two years from the closing date.

The offering remains subject to the receipt of all necessary regulatory approvals, including approval from the Canadian Securities Exchange, the release said, with closing expected on or about November 4, 2026. Securities issued under it will be subject to a four-month-and-one-day hold period from closing. The release did not name an agent, underwriter or finder for the offering, or disclose whether any insiders are participating.

The company said it intends to use the proceeds for exploration and for general working capital purposes. Beyond that, the disclosure in this release is limited: it does not specify which exploration program or property the funds are earmarked for, or provide a budget breakdown between exploration and working capital.

entries.headline: Fewer young women meet activity guidelines, Statistics Canada reports
entries.dek: Statistics Canada's October Health Reports found that 46% of Canadian adults met weekly activity guidelines, with activity trends diverging by age and sex.
entries.caption: Statistics Canada's October Health Reports tracked physical-activity trends among Canadian adults from 2007 to 2024, measured by accelerometer.
brief: Statistics Canada reported in its October 2026 Health Reports that 46% of Canadian adults met the recommendation of at least 150 minutes of moderate-to-vigorous physical activity per week, using accelerometer-measured data from the Canadian Health Measures Survey. The agency said the share of men aged 18 to 39 meeting the recommendation held stable at 65% from 2007 to 2024.

Over the same period, the share of women aged 18 to 39 meeting the recommendation fell from 52% to 43%, Statistics Canada said. Adults aged 60 to 79 moved the other way, with the share meeting the recommendation rising nine percentage points for both sexes between 2007 and 2024.

The agency also reported that from 2022 to 2024, 34% of women aged 18 to 39 needed only 5 to 10 more daily minutes to meet the recommendation, while 50% of women aged 60 to 79 logged under 10 qualifying minutes a day. About a third of adults recorded at least 7,500 steps daily over the period.
body: Statistics Canada published Health Reports for October 2026 on October 21, 2026, reporting that 46% of Canadian adults met the public health recommendation of at least 150 minutes of moderate-to-vigorous physical activity per week. The figures are drawn from accelerometer-measured data collected through the Canadian Health Measures Survey, which the agency said allows tracking of population-level activity trends over time, covering the period from 2007 to 2024.

The agency said the share of men aged 18 to 39 meeting the recommendation held stable at 65% across that period, from 2007 to 2024. Over the same seventeen years, the share of women aged 18 to 39 meeting the recommendation declined, from 52% to 43%, according to the release. Statistics Canada did not state a reason for the divergence between the two groups.

Adults aged 60 to 79 moved in the opposite direction from the youngest cohort of women: the agency reported a nine-percentage-point increase in the share meeting the recommendation for both men and women in that age group between 2007 and 2024. The release did not provide the specific starting and ending percentages for this age group, only the size of the increase.

Statistics Canada said that knowing the share of adults who meet the 150-minute threshold does not tell the whole story, because it also matters how close those who fall short are to reaching it. The agency therefore also measured, for 2022 to 2024, the gap between non-compliant adults' actual activity levels and the recommended threshold.

Over that 2022-to-2024 period, 34% of women aged 18 to 39 needed only 5 to 10 additional minutes of activity a day to meet the recommendation, the agency said. Among women aged 60 to 79, 50% were getting less than 10 qualifying minutes of activity a day over the same period.

The release also reported that, from 2022 to 2024, approximately one-third of Canadian adults recorded at least 7,500 steps a day, with minimal differences between men and women on that measure over the period. The agency did not report a corresponding steps-based figure for 2007, so no comparable trend over time is available for step counts.
